skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest mass on CT to determine if it represents a recurrence of a rib-associated tumor (e.g., hemangiopericytoma) versus a primary lung or diaphragmatic lesion.
steps: Identify the anatomical location of the soft tissue mass, specifically checking for adjacency to the thoracic cage (ribs) versus the lung parenchyma or diaphragm.
Inspect the interface between the mass and the adjacent rib bone for signs of osseous destruction, such as cortical erosion, lysis, or permeative changes.

Distinguish rib-origin recurrences (which typically show direct bone invasion/destruction) from epidiaphragmatic masses (smooth margins, no bone involvement) or subpleural lung nodules (spiculated margins, distinct from rib cortex).
